\input{tikz/fig_header.tex}

% The current mode DAC of dac_i again, with the switch drive tied down.
%
% V_bias is a constant, generated by the cascode device in the reference
% branch, and the bit and its complement swing about it rather than rail to
% rail. That is the point of the slide: the steering pair only has to move
% its gates far enough either side of V_bias to hand the tail current from
% one leg to the other, and a smaller swing about a fixed level disturbs the
% tail node — and so the settling — far less than a full swing does.
%
% The inset says what the rail is for: it is the level the drive swings
% about, not a gate that is held anywhere.
%
% The cell is drawn once, boxed, and the boxes that follow it are the same
% cell again — the array is N copies of one drawing, sized 1, 2, 4 ... N.
% The original leaves this to a row of dots between two slices.

\begin{circuitikz}[american, thick, transform shape, circuit ee IEC]

  \input{tikz/ckt_lib.tex}
  \input{tikz/rdac_lib.tex}

  \def\ytail{0.6}       % source of the tail devices
  \def\ypair{3.4}       % source of the steering pairs
  \def\ydrain{5.4}      % drain of the steering pairs
  \def\yplus{6.6}       % dummy rail, into the + input
  \def\yminus{7.8}      % summing rail, into the - input
  \def\ybias{2.6}       % the V_bias rail
  \def\xref{0}
  \def\dw{0.85}         % half the spacing of a steering pair

  % ---- Reference branch: a current source into a cascoded mirror ----
  \draw (\xref,\ytail) to [Tnmos, n=M0] (\xref,{\ytail+1.6});
  \draw (\xref,\ytail) -- ++(0,-0.3) \vground;
  \draw (\xref,{\ytail+1.6}) to [Tnmos, n=MC] (\xref,{\ytail+3.2});
  \draw (\xref,{\ytail+3.2}) to [I, invert] (\xref,{\ytail+5.0});
  \draw (\xref,{\ytail+5.0}) \vsupply;
  \draw (M0.gate) -| (\xref,{\ytail+1.6});
  \fill (\xref,{\ytail+1.6}) circle (0.07);

  % The cascode gate is the constant the drive swings about.
  \draw (MC.gate) -- ++(-0.9,0) coordinate (vbport);
  \rdacPort{(vbport)}{south east}{$V_{bias}$}

  % ---- One DAC cell, drawn once ----
  % #1 x origin, #2 suffix for the node names, #3 the device size label
  \newcommand{\dacCell}[3]{%
    \draw (#1,\ytail) to [Tnmos, n=MT#2] (#1,{\ytail+1.6});
    \draw (#1,\ytail) -- ++(0,-0.3) \vground;
    \draw (#1,{\ytail+1.6}) -- (#1,\ypair);
    \node[anchor=west] at ($(#1,{\ytail+2.1})+(0.25,0)$) {#3};
    \draw ({#1-\dw},\ypair) -- ({#1+\dw},\ypair);
    \draw ({#1-\dw},\ypair) to [Tnmos, n=ML#2] ({#1-\dw},\ydrain);
    \draw ({#1+\dw},\ypair) to [Tnmos, n=MR#2, mirror] ({#1+\dw},\ydrain);
    % Labels sit above their stubs so they stay inside the cell boundary.
    \draw (ML#2.gate) -- ++(-0.6,0);
    \node[anchor=south] at ($(ML#2.gate)+(-0.3,0.08)$) {$b_{#2}$};
    \draw (MR#2.gate) -- ++(0.6,0);
    \node[anchor=south] at ($(MR#2.gate)+(0.3,0.08)$) {$\overline{b_{#2}}$};
    % b steers into the summing rail, b-bar into the dummy rail.
    \draw ({#1-\dw},\ydrain) -- ({#1-\dw},\yminus);
    \fill ({#1-\dw},\yminus) circle (0.07);
    \draw ({#1+\dw},\ydrain) -- ({#1+\dw},\yplus);
    \fill ({#1+\dw},\yplus) circle (0.07);
    % The cell boundary.
    \draw[dashed, thin] ({#1-2.35},{\ytail-0.75}) rectangle ({#1+2.35},{\ydrain+0.55});
  }

  % An empty cell boundary: the same drawing again, left blank.
  \newcommand{\dacGhost}[1]{%
    \draw[dashed, thin] ({#1-2.35},{\ytail-0.75}) rectangle ({#1+2.35},{\ydrain+0.55});
    \node at (#1,{0.5*(\ytail+\ydrain)}) {$\cdots$};
  }

  \dacCell{4.8}{n}{$N$}
  \dacGhost{9.9}
  \dacCell{15.0}{0}{$1$}

  \node[anchor=north, align=center] at (9.9,{\ytail-1.1})
    {$N$ copies of the same cell, sized $1, 2, 4 \ldots N$};

  % ---- The gate rail every cell's tail device sits on ----
  \draw (M0.gate) -- (MTn.gate);
  \draw (MTn.gate) -- (MT0.gate);
  \fill (MTn.gate) circle (0.07);

  % ---- The two rails into the amplifier ----
  \draw ({4.8-\dw},\yminus) -- (18.8,\yminus);
  \draw ({4.8+\dw},\yplus) -- (18.8,\yplus);
  \rdacAmp{OA}{(18.8,7.2)}
  \draw (18.8,\yminus) -- (OAinn);
  \draw (18.8,\yplus) -- (OAinp);

  % ---- The dummy rail is held at a reference voltage ----
  \draw (18.1,\yplus) to [V] (18.1,{\yplus-2.2});
  \draw (18.1,{\yplus-2.2}) -- ++(0,-0.3) \vground;
  \fill (18.1,\yplus) circle (0.07);

  % ---- Feedback resistor over the top ----
  \draw (18.2,\yminus) -- (18.2,10.4) -- ++(0.7,0) \hresistor{$R_F$} -- ++(0.7,0)
        -- (22.0,10.4) -- (22.0,7.2) -- (OAout);
  \fill (18.2,\yminus) circle (0.07);
  \draw (OAout) -- ++(0.9,0);

  % ---- Inset: what V_bias is for ----
  \begin{scope}[shift={(3.6,9.2)}]
    \draw[dashed] (0,0.55) -- (4.4,0.55) node[anchor=west] {$V_{bias}$};
    \draw[thick] (0,1.15) -- (1.1,1.15) -- (1.1,-0.05) -- (2.2,-0.05)
                 -- (2.2,1.15) -- (3.3,1.15) -- (3.3,-0.05) -- (4.4,-0.05);
    \node[anchor=east] at (-0.15,0.55) {$b_n$};
    \node[anchor=north, align=center] at (2.2,-0.35)
      {the drive swings about $V_{bias}$, not rail to rail};
  \end{scope}

\end{circuitikz}
\end{document}
